# WIRE PROTOCOL frame-kind tokens the engine legitimately spells as string
# literals.
#
# These are subtracted from donor_names.txt before TestNoDonorLiteralsInEngine-
# Sources runs, exactly like schema_keywords.txt. They are `kind` values of the
# STREAM FRAMING — the protocol every consumer on the other side of the socket
# parses, identical on every robot — that happen to collide with a word one
# donor also uses for a channel.
#
# The bar for adding a line here, and it is deliberately narrower than
# schema_keywords.txt's:
#
#   1. the literal is a frame `kind` token of internal/stream's wire protocol,
#      spelled the same way for Reachy Mini, MicroDuck and a toy fixture alike;
#   2. it is used ONLY as that token — never to name a channel, an action, or a
#      sense field.
#
# A CHANNEL NAME OR AN ACTION NAME MAY NOT BE EXEMPTED HERE ON ANY GROUNDS.
# That a token listed below is also some robot's channel name is the collision
# this file records, not a licence to compile that robot's vocabulary into the
# engine: the engine still learns every channel, sense and action from an
# adaptor config, and a literal used as a robot name is a leak whatever file it
# is listed in. Every entry carries its justification on the line above it.

# `pose` is internal/stream's pose-frame `kind` — the token a consumer matches
# to recognise "here is the complete target the engine composed this tick"
# (stream.KindPose, pinned by TestPoseKindIsTheDeclaredWireToken). It collides
# with microduck's `pose` channel. The engine never names that channel: the
# only thing it spells is the frame kind, and a wire token the engine could not
# write down would be a protocol nobody could implement.
pose
